final_message:
I've written the revised sourcing and nomination workflow as a Word document (draft v0.1, for CPO review). I couldn't render it here, so the length is an estimate: about 2.5 pages, roughly 1,930 words.

The reference, workspace and attachment folders were empty, so there was no registry or operative record to check. The draft is built only from your brief, and it says so in its assumptions section.

**What the document covers:**
1. **Problem and objective:** why lamp design changes after nomination reopen the whole cycle and add up to 50% to timelines, and the four ways the new workflow deals with that.
2. **Modular quotation structure:** suppliers quote in seven cost modules instead of one lump-sum price. These are raw material (linked to a commodity index), child parts, features, design elements, process/conversion, tooling (inserts priced separately) and overheads. The negotiated lines become a rate card fixed at nomination, and a variant's price is the base plus whichever option modules it uses. Each TRSO feature is tagged to its modules, so a TRSO change shows its cost impact straight away.
3. **Process steps S1–S6 with gates G1–G4:** TRSO approval, supplier shortlist, an automatic quote-completeness check, and nomination. At nomination, Finance and Program Managers also approve the rate card and a range of pre-approved changes.
4. **Handling changes after nomination:** every change needs an updated TRSO signed by ER, Quality and Purchase. The price approval then depends on the size of the change:

| Class | When it applies | Who approves the price | Target time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minor | Rate-card items only, price change ≤2%, no safety impact | Purchase only (Finance and PM approved it in advance at nomination) | 2 working days |
| Moderate | 2–5% change, a new cost line, or a tooling change | Purchase, Finance and PM | 5 working days |
| Major | Over 5%, total change since nomination over 8%, any safety or homologation impact, or a change of supplier or location | Purchase, Finance and PM, then the CPO | 10 working days |

   It also adds six ways to keep work moving:
   - options quoted up front;
   - raw-material prices that follow an index instead of being renegotiated;
   - insert-level tooling;
   - a capped "proceed at risk" option while approval is pending;
   - parallel approvals with deadlines and escalation;
   - combining several open changes on the same part into one request.
5. **Approval matrix:** who approves, is consulted or is informed at each gate, for ER, Quality, Purchase, Finance, Program Managers and the CPO.
6. **Platform blueprint for TechSol:** eight components, the core data objects, links to PLM and ERP, and legally valid e-signatures.
7. **Rollout and open points:** a pilot on lamp assemblies, success measures, assumptions and open points.

**What still needs deciding:**
- **Thresholds and turnaround times are my proposals, not approved policy.** That covers the 2%, 5% and 8% limits and the 2/5/10-day times. Finance, Quality and the CPO need to ratify them before TechSol sets them as live defaults.
- **Supplier scorecard weights are not defined yet.** I didn't make them up; the draft says Purchase will propose them with ER and Quality.
- **The CPO's sign-off at nomination follows the existing delegation of authority.** That isn't in the inputs, so the draft refers to it without reproducing it.
- **Other decisions are left open on purpose.** These are the ERP and PLM system names, the improvement target, e-signature validation by Legal, and Quality's definition of a safety-relevant lamp change. The target waits until the pilot has measured a baseline.

Before finishing, I re-read the change classes, approval matrix and flexibility rules against each other and fixed four inconsistencies. For example, the class rules use "or" and now say which class is tested first. Raw-material index changes are now excluded from the percentage limits.
